records.context: A bounded five-second join used to let the screen disappear while the daemon independent execution path still owned a live SQLite connection.  That is unsafe at application shutdown: CPython can finalize the sqlite extension while the independent execution path is still inside it.  SQLite already bounds lock waits with its 30-second connection timeout, so a requested blocking stop waits for the independent execution path to close its cursor and connection completely.
records.label: spacr.qt.annotate_engine.SaveWorker.stop#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A bounded five-second join used to let the screen disappear while the daemon thread still owned a live SQLite connection.  That is unsafe at application shutdown: CPython can finalize the sqlite extension while the thread is still inside it.  SQLite already bounds lock waits with its 30-second connection timeout, so a requested blocking stop waits for the thread to close its cursor and connection completely.
records.translation: पहले सीमित पाँच-सेकंड join स्क्रीन को तब गायब होने देता था जब daemon थ्रेड के पास अब भी live SQLite connection होता था।  एप्लिकेशन बंद होते समय यह असुरक्षित है: CPython sqlite extension को तब finalize कर सकता है जब थ्रेड अब भी उसके भीतर हो।  SQLite पहले से अपने 30-सेकंड connection timeout से lock प्रतीक्षा सीमित करता है, इसलिए अनुरोधित blocking stop थ्रेड के अपना cursor और connection पूरी तरह बंद करने की प्रतीक्षा करता है।

records.context: Compared with ``==``, not ``is``. The pattern this module documents — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in the constructor and ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in ``closeEvent`` — hands over a *different bound-method object* each time, because Python builds a new one on every attribute access. Under an identity check that made every withdrawal a silent no-op, so the process-wide registry kept a reference to a destroyed application view and the next ``open_objects`` reached it. Bound methods compare equal exactly when their ``__self__`` and ``__func__`` match, which is the question being asked; anything that does not define ``__eq__`` (a lambda, a ``partial``) still falls back to identity, so the two-application view guarantee above is unchanged.

records.source: Compared with ``==``, not ``is``. The pattern this module documents — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in the constructor and ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in ``closeEvent`` — hands over a *different bound-method object* each time, because Python builds a new one on every attribute access. Under an identity check that made every withdrawal a silent no-op, so the process-wide registry kept a reference to a destroyed screen and the next ``open_objects`` reached it. Bound methods compare equal exactly when their ``__self__`` and ``__func__`` match, which is the question being asked; anything that does not define ``__eq__`` (a lambda, a ``partial``) still falls back to identity, so the two-screen guarantee above is unchanged.
records.translation: ``==`` से तुलना, ``is`` से नहीं। यह मॉड्यूल जिस pattern को दर्ज करता है — constructor में ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` और ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)``, जो ``closeEvent`` में है — हर बार एक *अलग bound-method object* देता है, क्योंकि Python हर attribute access पर नया बनाता है। पहचान जाँच में इससे हर वापसी चुपचाप no-op बन जाती थी, इसलिए प्रक्रिया-व्यापी registry नष्ट स्क्रीन का संदर्भ रखती रही और अगला ``open_objects`` उस तक पहुँच गया। bound methods ठीक तब बराबर होते हैं जब उनके ``__self__`` और ``__func__`` मेल खाते हैं, और यही पूछा जा रहा प्रश्न है; जो कुछ भी ``__eq__`` परिभाषित नहीं करता (एक lambda, एक ``partial``) वह अब भी पहचान पर लौटता है, इसलिए ऊपर की दो-स्क्रीन गारंटी अपरिवर्तित है।

records.context: This is the tool a brush is not. records.context: the session's :class:`spacr.curation.CurationLog` for this microscope field of view. Given one holding at least one edit, it is written to ``<mask>.curation.json`` beside the mask, so :func:`spacr.curation.is_curated` reports the saved mask as hand-edited. The log is written whole, so it must have been seeded from :meth:`CurationLog.read_beside` to keep earlier sessions' entries -- which is what the screen does on load. A log with no edits writes no sidecar: a session that opened the editor and painted nothing has not curated anything, and a ledger that exists for every mask ever opened answers no question.

records.translation: Settings CSVs दो-कॉलम ``Key,Value`` format में लिखी जाती हैं, जो `spacr.qt.screens.app_screen.AppScreen ._load_settings_csv` द्वारा आज़माई जाने वाली header जोड़ियों में पहली है, इसलिए "Import settings…" बटन हर मान को form में पुनर्स्थापित करता है। इनमें से किसी को सीधे Python से पढ़ने के लिए कॉलमों के नाम देने पड़ते हैं — ``load_settings(path, setting_key="Key", setting_value="Value")`` — क्योंकि `spacr.utils.load_settings` *डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से* दूसरी वर्तनी (``setting_key``/``setting_value``, जो `spacr.io.save_settings_to_db` लिखता है) उपयोग करता है और अनुमान लगाने के बजाय अपवाद उठाता है।

records.context: 1. ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files`` names its stack files ``<plate>_<well>_<field>.npy`` when ``timelapse=True`` — dropping the timeID and max-projecting every timepoint of a microscope field of view into one array — while ``spacr.io._generate_time_lists`` groups on ``<plate>_<well>_<field>_<time>.npy`` and skips anything with fewer than four underscore-separated parts. An 8-frame microscope field of view becomes one ``stack/plate1_A01_1.npy``, ``_generate_time_lists`` returns ``[]``, no ``*_norm_timelapse.npz`` is written, no masks are generated, and ``preprocess_generate_masks`` dies in ``_pivot_counts_table`` on ``no such table: object_counts``. Emitting the timeID in both branches (the non-timelapse spelling is already exactly what ``_generate_time_lists`` parses) is the fix. 2. Past that, ``spacr.object.generate_cellpose_masks_sam`` hands ``spacr.timelapse._trackpy_track_cells`` a **list** of 2-D frames, and the tracking chain indexes it as an array: ``_track_by_iou`` does ``masks.shape[0]`` and ``_relabel_masks_based_on_tracks`` does ``np.zeros(masks.shape, …)``, both ``AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'``. In the ``timelapse_mode='iou'`` path this demo asks for, the first one is swallowed by the ``except Exception`` retry loop in ``_facilitate_trackin_with_adaptive_removal``, which then shrinks the search range 100 times and reports ``Failed to track after 100 attempts`` — a message about displacement for a bug about a type. Coercing once at the top of ``_trackpy_track_cells`` (``masks = np.asarray(masks)``) clears both.
records.label: spacr.qt.synthetic.generate_timelapse_demo#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files`` names its stack files ``<plate>_<well>_<field>.npy`` when ``timelapse=True`` — dropping the timeID and max-projecting every timepoint of a field into one array — while ``spacr.io._generate_time_lists`` groups on ``<plate>_<well>_<field>_<time>.npy`` and skips anything with fewer than four underscore-separated parts. An 8-frame field becomes one ``stack/plate1_A01_1.npy``, ``_generate_time_lists`` returns ``[]``, no ``*_norm_timelapse.npz`` is written, no masks are generated, and ``preprocess_generate_masks`` dies in ``_pivot_counts_table`` on ``no such table: object_counts``. Emitting the timeID in both branches (the non-timelapse spelling is already exactly what ``_generate_time_lists`` parses) is the fix. 2. Past that, ``spacr.object.generate_cellpose_masks_sam`` hands ``spacr.timelapse._trackpy_track_cells`` a **list** of 2-D frames, and the tracking chain indexes it as an array: ``_track_by_iou`` does ``masks.shape[0]`` and ``_relabel_masks_based_on_tracks`` does ``np.zeros(masks.shape, …)``, both ``AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'``. In the ``timelapse_mode='iou'`` path this demo asks for, the first one is swallowed by the ``except Exception`` retry loop in ``_facilitate_trackin_with_adaptive_removal``, which then shrinks the search range 100 times and reports ``Failed to track after 100 attempts`` — a message about displacement for a bug about a type. Coercing once at the top of ``_trackpy_track_cells`` (``masks = np.asarray(masks)``) clears both.
records.translation: 1. ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files`` अपनी stack फ़ाइलों को ``<plate>_<well>_<field>.npy`` नाम देता है जब ``timelapse=True`` हो — timeID छोड़कर और किसी field के हर timepoint को एक array में max-project करके — जबकि ``spacr.io._generate_time_lists`` ``<plate>_<well>_<field>_<time>.npy`` पर समूहित करता है और चार से कम underscore-से-अलग हिस्सों वाली किसी भी चीज़ को छोड़ देता है। 8-frame field एक ``stack/plate1_A01_1.npy`` बन जाता है, ``_generate_time_lists`` ``[]`` लौटाता है, कोई ``*_norm_timelapse.npz`` नहीं लिखा जाता, कोई masks नहीं बनते, और ``preprocess_generate_masks`` ``_pivot_counts_table`` में ``no such table: object_counts`` पर मर जाता है। दोनों शाखाओं में timeID देना (गैर-timelapse वर्तनी पहले से ठीक वही है जो ``_generate_time_lists`` पार्स करता है) सुधार है। 2. उसके आगे, ``spacr.object.generate_cellpose_masks_sam`` ``spacr.timelapse._trackpy_track_cells`` को 2-D frames की **सूची** देता है, और tracking श्रृंखला उसे array की तरह index करती है: ``_track_by_iou`` ``masks.shape[0]`` करता है और ``_relabel_masks_based_on_tracks`` ``np.zeros(masks.shape, …)`` करता है, दोनों ``AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'``। इस demo द्वारा माँगे गए ``timelapse_mode='iou'`` पथ में पहला ``except Exception`` retry loop में निगल लिया जाता है, जो ``_facilitate_trackin_with_adaptive_removal`` में है, जो फिर खोज सीमा 100 बार घटाता है और ``Failed to track after 100 attempts`` बताता है — एक type के बग के लिए विस्थापन के बारे में संदेश। ``_trackpy_track_cells`` के शीर्ष पर एक बार रूपांतरण (``masks = np.asarray(masks)``) दोनों को ठीक करता है।

records.context: Re-entrant calls on the same thread are refused. Drawing a line runs Python inside a QWidget, and with verbose logging on the function-trace profile hook logs on entry to every spaCR function it passes through — including this one. Both console log sinks feed that record straight back here, and ``_StdoutBlock.append`` answers it with a nested ``setPlainText`` whose first act is to destroy the QTextDocument's frames — the ones the outer call is still inside. gdb: ``QTextFrame::~QTextFrame -> QTextDocumentPrivate::clear``, ``#0`` in freed memory. Reproduced as ``pytest tests/qt/test_all_module_smoke.py tests/qt/test_batch_f_diagnostics.py`` (exit 139).

records.context: There is deliberately no ``QThread.terminate()`` fallback. It used to be here, described as a last resort, and it was reached far more often than "last resort" suggests: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` queued `worker.finished -> thread.quit` to the GUI-affine QThread object, so the event that stops the independent execution path sat behind this method's own `wait()` and the wait timed out on streams that had already finished. Terminating an independent execution path that is executing Python is `pthread_cancel`: if it dies holding the GIL the process stops making progress with every independent execution path still alive, and if it dies inside Qt or PySide the heap is corrupt and the crash lands somewhere unrelated later. `bridge.drain_thread` parks an independent execution path that will not stop instead, which keeps the "never destroy an executing QThread" rule without buying it with undefined behaviour.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: There is deliberately no ``QThread.terminate()`` fallback. It used to be here, described as a last resort, and it was reached far more often than "last resort" suggests: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` queued `worker.finished -> thread.quit` to the GUI-affine QThread object, so the event that stops the thread sat behind this method's own `wait()` and the wait timed out on streams that had already finished. Terminating a thread that is running Python is `pthread_cancel`: if it dies holding the GIL the process stops making progress with every thread still alive, and if it dies inside Qt or PySide the heap is corrupt and the crash lands somewhere unrelated later. `bridge.drain_thread` parks a thread that will not stop instead, which keeps the "never destroy a running QThread" rule without buying it with undefined behaviour.
records.translation: जानबूझकर कोई ``QThread.terminate()`` fallback नहीं है। पहले यह यहाँ था, अंतिम उपाय के रूप में वर्णित, और "last resort" (अंतिम उपाय) जितना बताता है उससे कहीं अधिक बार इस तक पहुँचा जाता था: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` ने `worker.finished -> thread.quit` को GUI-affine QThread object पर queue किया, इसलिए थ्रेड रोकने वाला event इस method के अपने `wait()` के पीछे रुका रहता था और पहले ही पूरी हो चुकी streams पर wait का समय समाप्त हो जाता था। Python चला रहे थ्रेड को terminate करना `pthread_cancel` है: यदि वह GIL पकड़े मरता है तो हर थ्रेड जीवित रहते प्रक्रिया आगे बढ़ना बंद कर देती है, और यदि वह Qt या PySide के भीतर मरता है तो heap दूषित होता है और crash बाद में किसी असंबंधित जगह होता है। `bridge.drain_thread` इसके बजाय न रुकने वाले थ्रेड को park करता है, जो "never destroy a running QThread" नियम को अपरिभाषित व्यवहार की कीमत चुकाए बिना बनाए रखता है।

records.context: The first "→ Starting ..." notice of a session cost 33 ms on the main GUI execution path, almost all of it Qt looking up a fallback font for the arrow at the console's size; the same text costs 0.5 ms after that. The lookup is cached per independent execution path and per size, so it can only be done here, on the main GUI execution path, ahead of the notice: a processing session waiting on its workflow's import calls this while the busy bar is already showing. The font is taken from a stand-in entry, because the one an entry draws with carries the family list its sheet gives it, and a font that differs only in that list is a different cache entry.

records.context: The target is a misiurewicz point, preperiod 4 period 1, refined at startup by solving ``f_c^5(0) = f_c^4(0)``. A boundary point keeps revealing structure at any magnification.

records.translation: स्थिर `speed`, जब तक `variable_speed` चालू न हो, तब यह `speed_min` और `speed_max` के बीच घूमती है -- छिपे प्रतिशत के बजाय नामित सीमाएँ, ताकि यात्रा वास्तव में क्या करेगी यह देखकर अनुमान लगाने के बजाय सेटिंग्स से पढ़ा जा सके। `speed_period` एक पूरे चक्र में लगने वाला समय है, जो "how gradually" (कितनी धीरे-धीरे) नियंत्रण है: बड़ी संख्या धीमा परिवर्तन (CHANGE) है, धीमा fractal नहीं।

records.source: TWO PATTERNS ARE GPU-ONLY. Mandelbrot needs a texture of the reference orbit and a shader to perturb around it, and `orbit_gpu` is a fragment shader with no numba twin -- the CPU orbit fold is a DIFFERENT picture, four samples across four frames rather than four of one instant, which is why the two are separate entries at all.
records.translation: दो patterns केवल ग्राफ़िक्स कार्ड पर चलते हैं (TWO PATTERNS ARE GPU-ONLY)। Mandelbrot को reference orbit का texture और उसके चारों ओर perturb करने के लिए shader चाहिए, और `orbit_gpu` ऐसा fragment shader है जिसका कोई numba जुड़वाँ नहीं -- CPU orbit fold एक अलग (DIFFERENT) चित्र है, एक क्षण के चार के बजाय चार frames में चार samples, इसी कारण दोनों अलग प्रविष्टियाँ हैं।

records.context: spaCR measurement tables run to 10^5–10^6 object rows and a scatter of a million overlapping points is unreadable. Three strategies, chosen by what the plot needs, and **the chosen one is always named in** :attr:`RenderData.notice` so a subset can never be mistaken for the whole:

records.source: spaCR measurement tables run to 10^5–10^6 object rows and a scatter of a million overlapping points is unreadable. Three strategies, chosen by what the plot needs, and **the chosen one is always named in** :attr:`RenderData.notice` so a subset can never be mistaken for the whole:
records.translation: spaCR measurement तालिकाएँ 10^5–10^6 object पंक्तियों तक जाती हैं और दस लाख एक-दूसरे पर चढ़े बिंदुओं का scatter अपठनीय होता है। तीन रणनीतियाँ, plot की आवश्यकता के अनुसार चुनी गईं, और **चुनी गई रणनीति हमेशा इसमें नामित होती है:** :attr:`RenderData.notice`, ताकि किसी उपसमूह को कभी पूरा न समझा जाए:

records.context: **aggregate plots use every row, always.** A histogram, bar, box, violin or heatmap is already a reduction — sampling before aggregating would change the answer for no gain, so :data:`AGGREGATE_KINDS` never sample regardless of size.

records.source: spaCR measures hundreds of features per object. A PCA shows in one picture which measurements separate two populations, because the loadings say which measurements carry the separation.
records.translation: spaCR प्रति object सैकड़ों features मापता है। PCA एक चित्र में दिखाता है कि कौन-से measurements दो populations को अलग करते हैं, क्योंकि loadings बताती हैं कि अलगाव किन measurements में है।

records.context: A NaN in a spaCR measurement table is usually *structural*, not missing at random — the same reasoning :mod:`spacr.anndata_export` sets out at length. A ``pathogen_*`` column is NaN for a cell with no pathogen in it; that is a fact about the cell, not a gap in the record. Mean-imputing it invents a pathogen of average size and moves an uninfected cell into the middle of the infected distribution, invisibly.

records.source: A NaN in a spaCR measurement table is usually *structural*, not missing at random — the same reasoning :mod:`spacr.anndata_export` sets out at length. A ``pathogen_*`` column is NaN for a cell with no pathogen in it; that is a fact about the cell, not a gap in the record. Mean-imputing it invents a pathogen of average size and moves an uninfected cell into the middle of the infected distribution, invisibly.
records.translation: spaCR measurement तालिका में NaN सामान्यतः *संरचनात्मक* होता है, यादृच्छिक रूप से अनुपलब्ध नहीं — वही तर्क जिसे :mod:`spacr.anndata_export` विस्तार से बताता है। बिना pathogen वाली कोशिका के लिए ``pathogen_*`` कॉलम NaN होता है; यह कोशिका के बारे में तथ्य है, रिकॉर्ड में अंतराल नहीं। इसे mean से impute करना औसत आकार का pathogen गढ़ता है और असंक्रमित कोशिका को अदृश्य रूप से संक्रमित वितरण के बीच में ले जाता है।

records.context: :data:`NAN_AUTO`, the default, picks between the first two by how the missingness is shaped, because in this table the two shapes are far apart: a structural NaN affects tens of percent of the rows (every uninfected cell), a sporadic one affects a handful (one object where mahotas returned nothing). So a feature missing in more than :data:`DEFAULT_STRUCTURAL_MISSING` of the rows is treated as structural and dropped by name; rows still carrying a NaN among the survivors are dropped as sporadic and counted. Nothing is imputed, and both actions appear in :attr:`PCAResult.notes` and in :meth:`PCAResult.report`.

records.context: PCA maximises variance, and variance has units. In a spaCR object table ``cell_area`` is px² and runs to 10^4 with a variance near 10^6; ``eccentricity`` is dimensionless and lives in ``[0, 1]``; ``channel_1_mean_intensity`` is counts. An unscaled (covariance) PCA of those three returns "PC1 = cell_area" every time — not because size is the interesting axis but because px² is a big number. Worse, the answer is not even stable: recording the same areas in µm² instead of px² would rotate every component.

records.source: What "detection" means here, exactly
records.translation: यहाँ "detection" (पहचान) का ठीक-ठीक अर्थ क्या है

records.context: 1. **Count failed or non-converged fits as non-detections.** Do not drop them: that would inflate statistical power by removing executions whose design was too weak to fit. 2. **Report mean AUROC beside statistical power.** Calculate the mean over converged fits and also report how many fits failed or did not converge. Thus power 0/5 with five non-converged fits differs from power 0/5 with five converged fits at AUROC 0.52.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.power_design#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. **A replicate whose fit failed or did not converge counts as a non-detection**, not as a missing value. Dropping it would raise the reported power by removing exactly the runs where the design was too thin to fit — which is the failure mode the analysis is supposed to find. 2. **The mean AUROC is reported beside the power**, over the replicates that did converge, with the count of those that did not. A power of 0/5 with five non-converged fits and a power of 0/5 with five converged fits at AUROC 0.52 are different findings.
records.translation: 1. **जिस replicate का fit विफल हुआ या converge नहीं हुआ वह गैर-detection गिना जाता है**, अनुपलब्ध मान नहीं। उसे हटाने से ठीक वे रन हटेंगे जहाँ design fit के लिए बहुत पतला था, और इससे रिपोर्ट की गई power ऊँची हो जाएगी — और यही वह विफलता रूप है जिसे विश्लेषण को खोजना है। 2. **power के पास mean AUROC बताया जाता है**, converge हुए replicates पर, न converge होने वालों की गिनती के साथ। पाँच non-converged fits के साथ 0/5 की power और AUROC 0.52 पर पाँच converged fits के साथ 0/5 की power अलग निष्कर्ष हैं।

records.translation: :func:`enumerate_image_sets` इसकी जगह लेता है। यह ``os.scandir`` और प्रोजेक्ट के अपने acquisition regex (``spacr.utils._get_regex``) के माध्यम से **केवल फ़ाइल नाम** पढ़ता है, और उन्हें :class:`ImageSet` रिकॉर्डों में समूहित करता है, जो ``(plate, well, field)`` पर आधारित हैं, जिनमें हर एक से channel फ़ाइलें जुड़ी होती हैं। वह सूची बनाने के लिए कोई छवि खोली, decode या stack नहीं की जाती। फिर :func:`sample_image_sets` एक सीमित यादृच्छिक sample लेता है — डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से 20 sets, जिसे sets dropdown के ठीक बाईं ओर रखे :class:`FlatSpinBox` से बदला जा सकता है।

records.context: The sample is **random but reproducible**: the seed is a stable digest of ``"<folder name>|<total sets>|<cap>|<nonce>"`` (:func:`sample_seed`), so the same laboratory microplate at the same cap yields the same sets in this session, the next session, and on another machine or mount point — a preview can be described and returned to. It is deliberately *not* seeded from the clock or from ``hash()``, which is salted per process. Re-rendering never re-draws; only an explicit act does — changing the cap (which is in the seed) or calling :func:`~ImageSetSampler.reshuffle` (which bumps the nonce).

records.context: **Shared axes by default.** Two panels whose y axes differ by an order of magnitude look identical, so a per-panel autoscale turns "the knockdown halved the count" into "the two panels look the same". Every scale here is computed over the whole grid unless the user explicitly asks otherwise, and when they do ask otherwise :attr:`Trellis.notice` says so in words, so a free-scale trellis copied into a slide still states that its scales differ. :data:`SCALE_ROW` and :data:`SCALE_COL` are the middle grounds: panels down a column of the grid share, or panels across a row do, which is what you want when the rows are three different measurements and the columns are three conditions.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec#2

records.source: **Shared axes by default.** Two panels whose y axes differ by an order of magnitude look identical, so a per-panel autoscale turns "the knockdown halved the count" into "the two panels look the same". records.translation: **डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से साझा अक्ष।** जिन दो पैनलों के y अक्ष परिमाण के एक क्रम से भिन्न हैं वे एक जैसे दिखते हैं, इसलिए प्रति-पैनल autoscale "knockdown ने गिनती आधी कर दी" को "दोनों पैनल एक जैसे दिखते हैं" में बदल देता है। यहाँ हर scale पूरे grid पर गणना किया जाता है जब तक उपयोगकर्ता स्पष्ट रूप से अन्यथा न माँगे, और जब वे माँगते हैं तो :attr:`Trellis.notice` इसे शब्दों में कहता है, ताकि slide में कॉपी किया गया free-scale trellis भी बताए कि उसके scales भिन्न हैं। :data:`SCALE_ROW` और :data:`SCALE_COL` बीच के रास्ते हैं: grid के एक कॉलम में नीचे के पैनल साझा करते हैं, या एक पंक्ति के पार के पैनल, और यही आप चाहते हैं जब पंक्तियाँ तीन अलग measurements हों और कॉलम तीन स्थितियाँ।
